name: Bard

source.note: Entered from knowledge of the 2024 PHB; compare every number with the book before setting checked_against.

summary: A performer whose words and music carry magic: Bardic Inspiration lifts allies and a broad spell list covers almost any need.

recommended.note: Charisma first, then Dexterity for Armor Class in Light armor.

features.name: Bardic Inspiration
features.summary: Bonus Action: give a creature within 60 feet a Bardic Inspiration die (d6) to add to a D20 Test it fails.
features.text: As a Bonus Action you inspire another creature within 60 feet of you that can see or hear you; it gains one Bardic Inspiration die (a d6, growing at levels 5, 10 and 15). Once within the next hour, when it fails a D20 Test, it can roll the die and add the number, possibly turning the failure into a success. A creature can hold only one of these dice at a time. You can do this a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum once), regaining every use on a Long Rest (from level 5, on a Short Rest too).

features.name: Spellcasting
features.summary: Cast Bard spells with Charisma; two cantrips and four prepared spells to start.
features.text: You know two Bard cantrips (more at levels 4 and 10) and prepare level 1+ Bard spells for which you have slots, as many as the Prepared Spells column shows. Whenever you gain a Bard level you can replace one cantrip and one prepared spell with others from the Bard list. Charisma is your spellcasting ability, and a Musical Instrument can be your focus.

features.name: Expertise
features.summary: Expertise in two skills you're proficient in.
features.text: Choose two of your skill proficiencies; your Proficiency Bonus is doubled for ability checks that use them. You choose two more at Bard level 9.

features.name: Jack of All Trades
features.summary: Add half your Proficiency Bonus (round down) to skill checks you aren't proficient in.
features.text: When you make an ability check with a skill you lack proficiency in, and nothing else adds your Proficiency Bonus to it, you add half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down.

features.name: Bard Subclass
features.text: You choose a Bard subclass. From now on you gain each subclass feature when you reach its Bard level.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.summary: Gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat you qualify for.
features.text: Take the Ability Score Improvement feat (+2 to one ability or +1 to two, to a maximum of 20) or any other feat whose prerequisites you meet.

features.name: Font of Inspiration
features.summary: Bardic Inspiration comes back on a Short Rest too, and you can trade a spell slot for a use.
features.text: You regain all expended uses of Bardic Inspiration when you finish a Short or Long Rest. You can also expend a spell slot (no action required) to regain one use.

features.name: Subclass Feature
features.summary: Gain a feature from your Bard subclass.

features.name: Countercharm
features.summary: Reaction: a creature within 30 feet that fails a save against Charmed or Frightened rerolls it with Advantage.
features.text: When you or a creature within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw against an effect that applies the Charmed or Frightened condition, you can take a Reaction to let it reroll the save with Advantage on the new roll.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.summary: Gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat you qualify for.
features.text: Take the Ability Score Improvement feat (+2 to one ability or +1 to two, to a maximum of 20) or any other feat whose prerequisites you meet.

features.name: Expertise
features.summary: Expertise in two more skills you're proficient in.
features.text: Choose two more of your skill proficiencies to gain Expertise in.

features.name: Magical Secrets
features.summary: From now on your prepared spells can come from the Bard, Cleric, Druid and Wizard lists.
features.text: Secrets gathered from other traditions widen your repertoire. Whenever you gain a Bard level and may prepare more spells, and whenever you swap a prepared spell, the new spell can come from the Bard, Cleric, Druid or Wizard spell list. Spells chosen this way count as Bard spells for you.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.summary: Gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat you qualify for.
features.text: Take the Ability Score Improvement feat (+2 to one ability or +1 to two, to a maximum of 20) or any other feat whose prerequisites you meet.

features.name: Subclass Feature
features.summary: Gain a feature from your Bard subclass.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.summary: Gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat you qualify for.
features.text: Take the Ability Score Improvement feat (+2 to one ability or +1 to two, to a maximum of 20) or any other feat whose prerequisites you meet.

features.name: Superior Inspiration
features.summary: When you roll Initiative, regain Bardic Inspiration uses until you have at least two.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.summary: Gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat you qualify for.
features.text: Take an Epic Boon feat or any other feat whose prerequisites you meet. Boon of Spell Recall is recommended.

features.name: Words of Creation
features.summary: Power Word Heal and Power Word Kill are always prepared and can each target a second creature.
